caption: The drawing depicts a beaded sash or belt with fringed ends, laid out in an upside-down "V" shape against a solid black rectangular background. The sash features a geometric pattern consisting of diamond and rectangular shapes, rendered in a repeating sequence along its length. The colors used in the sash are primarily light blue, green, and white, with white beads outlining the diamond patterns and forming straight lines, while green and blue beads fill in the surrounding areas and add additional details. The fringed ends of the sash consist of strands of beads in blue, green, and white, hanging loosely with slight curves. The entire composition is centered inside the black rectangle, which itself is set within a border of plain off-white or light beige.
title: Bead Belt
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
